learning_objective: 🎯 Let us discover Personal, Possessive, and Demonstrative pronouns to make our sentences smart and avoid repeating names!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: These are the heroes that replace names of people or things! Words like I, you, he, she, it, we, and they are Personal Pronouns. Example: 'Ravi is playing' becomes 'He is playing'.
These pronouns show who owns something without using an apostrophe! Words like mine, yours, his, hers, and theirs. Example: 'This book is mine.'
These pointing pronouns show exactly which thing we are talking about. 'This' and 'These' are for things near us. 'That' and 'Those' are for things far away!

fun_activity.title: 👉 Point and Say
fun_activity.instructions: Point to something close to you and say 'This is my toy'. Then point to something far away and say 'That is a window'. Practice with These and Those too!

quick_recap: ⭐ Personal pronouns (I, she, they) take the place of nouns so we don't repeat names.
⭐ Possessive pronouns (mine, ours) show that something belongs to someone.
⭐ Demonstrative pronouns (this, that, these, those) point out specific things.
